topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture by linking to previous histopathology practicals and detailing the learning objectives for cancer cell biology.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed normal cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure malignant transformation.

topics.label: Classifications and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the operational categories of cancer genes and illustrate how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations disrupt pathways such as cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms and forms of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation give rise to sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the stepwise accumulation of mutations drives tumor development and clonal evolution in both sporadic and inherited cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary, recommended reading, and a preview of upcoming material.
